newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Richter reports rising margins for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Richter reports rising margins for 1996.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Vegyeszeti Gyar Rt said on Tuesday that its operating margin increased in 1996 over 1995 as a result of cost controls and increased sales efficiencies.

"Operating margins in 1996 increased to 24.7 percent from 20.9 percent in 1995, reflecting a continuation of the benefits highlighted in earlier quarterly reports, notably stringent cost management and increased efficiencies resulting from higher sales levels," Richter said in its earnings report. @

Richter released its 1996 IAS results this morning and said that its operating profit rose to 9.072 billion forints from 5.716 billion in 1995, while its sales grew to 36.764 billion forints in 1996 from 27.394 billion in 1995.
The company reported rising sales to all of its markets.
"Increases were achieved in each of the company's four main geographical areas - Hungary, Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Eastern Europe and the rest of the world." @

The company's domestic sales amounted to 12.125 billion forints last year, representing a 36.1 percent rise over the previous year, Richter said. It added that it retained its second place ranking in the Hungarian pharmaceuticals market with a 1996 market share of 9.8 percent.
Exports rose to 24.639 billion forints in 1996 from 18.482 billion in 1995 and represented 67 percent of total sales, the company said.
The biggest part, 10.536 billion forints, of total exports went to the CIS markets. @

"Good growth in sales, particularly in the second half of the year, was reported from most states, notably Russia and the Ukraine which represent the largest markets for the company's products," the report said.

"The strong distribution network continues to be a positive contributor to the company's market presence and whilst the general political and economic conditions remain uncertain, trading conditions remain stable." @

Richter added that the joint venture manufacturing company in Russia, established in mid-1996, continues to progress satisfactorily and while further investment is planned, it is expected that local operations will commence during 1997.
Richter's sales to eastern Europe rose to 5.446 billion forints from 3.903 billion in 1995, while its sales to what it calls the rest of the world rose to 8.657 billion from 7.061 billion in 1995.
